startup.platform: Desktop Chromium, 1280x720 default viewport, local TLS production build and real Core fixture. No mobile performance samples.
startup.measurement: usableMs is a browser DOM readiness proxy: document time origin for reload, captured click for navigation, first enabled destination control with layout rectangles that remains usable for two animation frames. The timestamp records the first candidate, not a confirmed presented frame. Controls render with ready data; full-page/scroll completion is not measured. Node wall time is separate. Loading text is polled every 20ms; zero observations does not prove absence of a brief loading frame.

startup.quietWindow: The other chat confirmed it paused heavy work. Quiet runs still exceeded 100ms, disproving contention as the sole explanation. Final9 runs followed a later change that renders public content during pending startup; they are not labelled quiet. Earlier outliers remain included.

profiling.limitations: Instrumented attribution runs, not SLO benchmarks. Frame markers are animation-frame callbacks, not proof of physical pixel presentation. The final viewport run overlapped unit/static checks and is not a controlled latency comparison. Different fixture aliases without seeded history caused two initial viewport test failures; the corrected seeded-history run passed three desktop sizes.

implementedAfterLastFullBenchmark: Per-phase server timing around initial entry, metadata, canonical history, final authority, encoding and admission.
Correction command Atom/runtime initialization deferred until the first write or recovery; read-only mount/dispose regression test passes.

desktopWorkflows.scope: Desktop workflows beyond reload and rapid sign-in/reload. Local production TLS build and real Core fixture: 500 Transactions, 16 Budgets, 10 Recurring plans and 50 Review items. No mobile samples.
desktopWorkflows.measurement: Browser click to first enabled control or data element with layout rectangles, confirmed stable across two animation frames. Month changes additionally require a changed month heading; Review selection requires the target row to be selected and its detail heading to match. This is a DOM-readiness proxy, not physical frame presentation. Each interaction has one sample per run; no reliable percentile claim.
desktopWorkflows.fix: Closed create-from-transaction and link-existing-transaction sections now mount the transaction picker on first expansion and retain it when closed. Opening a blank Recurring editor no longer reads Transactions. Existing eager disclosures retain their previous behavior. No server authorization, Consent, Audits, expiry, admission or rate-limit policy changed.
caveats: The first harness selected a group Budget editor, which has no amount input. Its timeout was a probe mistake. The corrected criterion observes the enabled actual editor form.

The initial before probe recorded two Review cached returns as 0ms because titles were identical and it checked readiness before the handler. Those two values are invalid. Later runs require the target row selection and wait for a DOM mutation.

The first expanded workflow run expected a read-only transaction value, but an editable transaction opens its correction form. Its final timeout was a probe mistake; the corrected criterion observes the actual enabled correction amount field.
Earlier first visits and a later first Recurring month change exceeded 100ms. Favorable single samples do not establish consistency.
Improvements outside the hidden-picker request count cannot be attributed to this UI patch from these separate local runs.

checks.regressionAfter: Focused real-Core desktop test passed: no hidden read, actual results on expansion, one total read after close/reopen.

reproduction.limitation: Historical timing harnesses ran from /tmp and are not part of the repository. Historical timings cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte from the final PR; preserve them as dated attribution evidence rather than an SLO assertion. The checked-in browser tests exercise ownership, request count, canonical authority and retained navigation.
